record.label: Late-layer error attribution vs offline MC truth
record.summary: Which mechanism owns the Q24 host's late-layer (l=10-15) mean error: marginal Edgeworth-truncation at the emission, pair/covariance state error echo, or non-Edgeworth width-finite remainder? Offline MC truth (weights-only, seeded, no sealed access) at per-unit SE below the q scale decides. This is the cheapest fatal gate: the winning mechanism defines which construction (higher-order closure with kappa5/kappa6 laws, late-layer rho/covariance repair, width-finite kernel correction, or late-layer FLOP reallocation) gets the one-arm build. VERDICT (2026-08-29, both rows, preregistered gates met): INGREDIENTS. The drifted pre-layer state carries the late-layer mean error - term B = 114/121 percent of noise-corrected energy on ranks 35/100; the order-2 emission formula at TRUE state errs BELOW the 8M-sample noise floor (term A negative after noise subtraction); the host-convention term C is zero to 8 decimals (which also validates tap alignment). MC noise 12/17 percent of raw. The formula-upgrade branch (kappa5 column) is dead for this purpose; the fight is state propagation accuracy. Ingredient sub-split (m vs v vs k3 vs k4) running from saved states.
record.terminal_criterion: Solved: ATTRIBUTION_rank0035/0100.json are the receipts; sub-split extends under G19B.

evidence.claim: late-layer mean error attribution: ingredients dominant, formula below noise
